challenge.exploration_summary: Explored the jwt library codebase. The Validator is the core validation engine with support for exp, iat, nbf, aud, iss, and sub claims. It uses functional ParserOption for configuration. The library supports both RegisteredClaims (struct) and MapClaims (map) claim types. The iat claim was only used for future-date checking (verifyIat), but there was no mechanism to enforce a maximum token age based on the iat claim — a common security pattern used to enforce token rotation policies.
challenge.feature_spec: Add max token age validation to the Validator. When configured with WithMaxAge(duration), the validator checks the iat (Issued At) claim and rejects tokens whose age exceeds the specified duration. The feature: (1) adds a maxAge field to the Validator struct, (2) adds a verifyMaxAge method that computes token age from the iat claim, (3) integrates the check into the Validate method, (4) adds a WithMaxAge parser option, (5) adds a new ErrTokenTooOld sentinel error, and (6) respects the existing leeway configuration for clock skew tolerance.
challenge.feature_rationale: This feature belongs in the validator module because max token age is a standard JWT validation concern closely related to the existing exp and iat checks. It leverages the existing iat claim infrastructure and follows the same patterns as the other verification methods (verifyExpiresAt, verifyIssuedAt, verifyNotBefore, etc.). The feature is useful for enforcing token rotation policies where tokens must be refreshed periodically regardless of their expiration time, which is a common security best practice.
challenge.bug_description: The Validate method passes v.maxAge + v.leeway to verifyMaxAge, but verifyMaxAge also adds v.leeway internally. This causes the leeway to be applied twice, effectively doubling the clock-skew tolerance for the maxAge check. A token that should be rejected (because it exceeds maxAge + leeway) is incorrectly accepted if it falls within the doubled-leeway window. This weakens the security of the maxAge enforcement by allowing tokens to live up to 2x the configured leeway tolerance.
